kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-01.title: Simplify
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-01.body:
Each fraction simplifies: $\frac{66}{77} = \frac67$, $\frac{555}{666} = \frac56$, $\frac{4444}{5555} = \frac45$, $\frac{33333}{44444} = \frac34$. All have the form $\frac{n-1}{n}$, i.e. $1 - \frac1n$, which is larger when $n$ is larger. So $\frac78$ (with $n = 8$) is the largest.

**Answer: (A) 7/8**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-02.title: Half of the daylight
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-02.body:
From 04:53 to 21:25 is 16 h 32 min. Half of that is 8 h 16 min, and $04{:}53 + 8{:}16 = 13{:}09$.

**Answer: (C) 13:09**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-02.title: Average the times
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-02.body:
In minutes after midnight: $04{:}53 = 293$ and $21{:}25 = 1285$. The average is $\frac{293+1285}{2} = 789$ minutes $= 13$ h 9 min.

**Answer: (C) 13:09**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-03.title: Divide with remainder
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-03.body:
$23 \cdot 87 = 2001$, one egg short of 2002. So he needs 88 days, giving $23\cdot88 = 2024$ eggs, and $2024 - 2002 = 22$ are left.

**Answer: (E) 88 days, 22 eggs left**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-04.title: Overlap
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-04.body:
Everyone speaks at least one language. Adding $85\% + 75\% = 160\%$ counts the bilingual people twice, so the bilingual part is $160\% - 100\% = 60\%$.

**Answer: (D) 60**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-04.title: Complements
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-04.body:
$15\%$ do not speak English (they speak only French) and $25\%$ do not speak French (only English). The rest, $100\% - 15\% - 25\% = 60\%$, speak both.

**Answer: (D) 60**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-05.title: Inclusion–exclusion
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-05.body:
Multiples of 3 up to 100: 33. Numbers ending in 3: $3, 13, \dots, 93$: 10. Counted twice (both): $3, 33, 63, 93$: 4. Claps: $33 + 10 - 4 = 39$.

**Answer: (D) 39**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-06.title: Test values
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-06.body:
If Andrew ate 6, the others ate at most 5 each, so at most $6 + 5 + 5 = 16 < 17$. If Andrew ate 7, the others can eat 5 and 5: $7 + 5 + 5 = 17$ ✓.

**Answer: (E) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-07.title: Bound and construction
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-07.body:
A coin covers its own square and at most 3 neighbours (in a 2-row grid a square has at most 3 side-neighbours): at most 4 squares. The grid has 18 squares, so at least $18/4$, i.e. at least 5 coins.

Five coins work: put them in columns 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, alternating top, bottom, top, bottom, top. Each coin covers the square below/above it and the neighbours in its row, and every square of the even columns is next to one of them.

**Answer: (A) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-08.title: Count pairs
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-08.body:
- Two circles: at most 2 points.
- Three lines: at most 3 points (one per pair).
- A line and a circle: at most 2 points, and there are $3\cdot2 = 6$ such pairs: 12 points.

With all points different: $2 + 3 + 12 = 17$.

**Answer: (B) 17**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-09.title: Each digit in each place
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-09.body:
There are $4! = 24$ numbers. In each position (thousands, hundreds, tens, units) each digit appears $24/4 = 6$ times, so each position contributes $6\cdot(1+2+3+4) = 60$ times its place value. Sum $= 60\cdot1111 = 66660$.

**Answer: (C) 66660**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-09.title: Pair numbers
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-09.body:
Pair each number with the one where each digit $d$ is replaced by $5 - d$ (e.g. 1234 with 4321). Each pair sums to $5555$, and there are 12 pairs: $12\cdot5555 = 66660$.

**Answer: (C) 66660**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-10.title: Halving twice
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-10.body:
Joining the midpoints of a rectangle's sides gives a rhombus with half its area, and joining the midpoints of the rhombus's sides gives a rectangle with half of that. So $KLMN$ is $\frac12$ and $OPRS$ is $\frac14$ of $ABCD$.

Grey = the four corners outside $KLMN$ ($\frac12$) plus $OPRS$ ($\frac14$): $\frac34$.

**Answer: (D) 3/4**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-11.title: Teeth passing
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-11.body:
Touching gears turn in opposite directions, so the small one turns clockwise. The same length of rim passes the contact point on both wheels. The large rim is 3 times as long, so one turn of the large wheel moves the small wheel's rim 3 times around.

**Answer: (B) turn around three times clockwise**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-12.title: Extra cost above 2 euros
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-12.body:
If all 8 boxes were apples they would cost 16 euros; the extra $7$ euros comes from pears (1 euro extra each) and plums (2 euros extra each). With $l$ plum boxes and $p$ pear boxes, $p + 2l = 7$, so $l \le 3$. $l = 3$, $p = 1$ and 4 apple boxes works: $8 + 3 + 12 = 23$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-13.title: Contradicting statements
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-13.body:
Christian and Daniel name different boys, so at least one of them lies — that is the only liar, and Alfred and Benjamin tell the truth. Benjamin did not do it, so Daniel's statement is the false one and Christian is right: Daniel hid the present.

**Answer: (D) Daniel**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-14.title: Use 11 litres
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-14.body:
11 litres of water become 12 litres of ice. Melting, 12 litres of ice shrink back to 11 litres: a decrease of 1 out of 12, i.e. $\frac{1}{12}$.

**Answer: (C) 1/12**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-16.title: Sundays alternate parity
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-16.body:
Consecutive Sundays are 7 days apart, so their dates alternate between odd and even. Three even Sundays need five Sundays in the month, with the 1st, 3rd and 5th even: the first Sunday is the 2nd, and the Sundays are 2, 9, 16, 23, 30. The 16th is a Sunday, so the 20th is a Thursday.

**Answer: (D) Thursday**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-17.title: Common value for b
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-17.body:
Make $b$ the same in both ratios: $a:b = 45:20$ and $b:c = 20:12$. Take $a = 45$, $b = 20$, $c = 12$: $(a-b):(b-c) = 25:8$.

**Answer: (B) 25:8**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-18.title: Each boy is weighed four times
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-18.body:
There are 10 pairs and each boy is in 4 of them. The sum of all pair weights is $90+92+93+94+95+96+97+98+100+101 = 956$, which is 4 times the total. Total $= 956 \div 4 = 239$ kg.

**Answer: (C) 239 kg**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-19.title: Compute each area
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-19.body:
Let each square have side 2 (area 4).

- $S_1$: the square joining the four midpoints: half of the square, 2.
- $S_2$: triangle with base the whole top side (2) and apex at the midpoint of the bottom side (height 2): $\frac12\cdot2\cdot2 = 2$.
- $S_3$: triangle with base from the bottom-left corner to the midpoint of the bottom side (1) and apex at the top-right corner (height 2): $\frac12\cdot1\cdot2 = 1$.
- $S_4$: parallelogram with horizontal sides of length 1 (top and bottom) and height 2: $1\cdot2 = 2$.

So $S_3 < S_1 = S_2 = S_4$.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-20.title: Add the rates
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-20.body:
Walking covers $\frac{1}{90}$ of the escalator per second and the escalator $\frac{1}{60}$. Together: $\frac{1}{90} + \frac{1}{60} = \frac{2+3}{180} = \frac{1}{36}$ per second, so it takes 36 seconds.

**Answer: (A) 36**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-20.title: Use a length
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-20.body:
Say the escalator has 180 steps. Walking: 2 steps/s; escalator: 3 steps/s; together 5 steps/s, so $180 \div 5 = 36$ s.

**Answer: (A) 36**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-21.title: Half of a smaller cylinder
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-21.body:
The glass has diameter $a$ and height $2a$. Tilted by $45^\circ$, the horizontal water surface goes from the lowest point of the rim of the base up to the opposite side at a distance $a$ along it (across the diameter $a$ it rises by $a$, since the slope is $45^\circ$).

So the water fills a piece of the bottom part of the glass of length $a$, and the slanted surface cuts that cylinder of height $a$ into two congruent halves. Water $= \frac12\cdot(\text{cylinder of height } a) = \frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot(\text{glass}) = \frac14$ of the glass.

**Answer: (B) 25%**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-22.title: Least common multiple
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-22.body:
$n$ is divisible by $\text{lcm}(21, 9) = 63 = 3^2\cdot7$, so every divisor of 63 divides $n$: $1, 3, 7, 9, 21, 63$ — six divisors. For $n = 63$ there are exactly these 6.

**Answer: (D) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-23.title: Write equations
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-23.body:
The three balances say: $C + B = A$, $B = D + C$ and $2A = 3D$.

From the first two, $A = B + C$ and $D = B - C$. Then $2(B + C) = 3(B - C)$, so $2B + 2C = 3B - 3C$ and $B = 5C$.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-23.title: Check with numbers
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-23.body:
Try $C = 1$, $B = 5$: then $A = 6$ and $D = 4$, and indeed $2A = 12 = 3D$. So B weighs as much as 5 weights C.

**Answer: (C) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-24.title: Face by face
kangaroo-ca-2002-g0708-24.body:
The three removed rows go straight through the centre of the cube, one in each direction, so each face has its centre square missing and a tunnel behind it.

- **On the outside faces:** a cube with exactly one painted face must be in the inner $3\times3$ part of a face. The centre is gone, and the 4 cubes next to the centre now also touch a tunnel wall (2 painted faces). That leaves the 4 corners of the inner $3\times3$ on each face: $6\cdot4 = 24$.
- **Inside the cube:** the inner $3\times3\times3$ block loses its centre and the 6 cubes around it (the tunnels). Of the 20 cubes left, the 8 corner ones touch no tunnel (no paint) and the other 12 each touch two tunnels (2 painted faces). None has exactly one.

Total: 24.

**Answer: (E) 24**
